content.title: About
content.content: Shiitake (Lentinula edodes) is an edible mushroom native to East Asia. It is cultivated on wood blocks and is known for its meaty flavor, nutty aroma, and firm texture. Shiitake is widely used in Asian cuisine, soups, stews, and vegetarian dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shiitake is considered the “king of mushrooms” in Japan and China.
The first commercial cultivation method was developed in Japan in the early 1920s.
The mushroom contains lentinan, a polysaccharide studied for its immune‑stimulating properties.
Dried shiitake can be stored for up to a year in a dry place.
In Japan, shiitake is often served tempura‑style, battered and fried.

items.title: Rich in beta‑glucans
items.content: Beta‑glucans support the immune system and may help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Shiitake is one of the few plant sources of vitamin D2, important for bone health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The mushroom provides niacin, riboflavin, and vitamin B6, which are involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Low‑calorie protein source
items.content: Dried shiitake offers about 20 g of protein per 100 g, making it a good addition to vegetarian diets.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Ergothioneine and ergothioneine in shiitake help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to shiitake.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: The mushroom contains purines, so people with gout should limit intake.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Shiitake contains modest amounts of oxalates, which may be a concern for kidney‑stone‑prone individuals.

items.title: Requires cooking
items.content: Raw shiitake may contain small amounts of toxins and should be cooked before consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Shiitake can be used fresh or dried. Dried mushrooms are re‑hydrated in warm water, then added to soups, sauces, stews, or stir‑fries. Fresh shiitake works well for quick sautéing, grilling, or adding to salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh shiitake in the refrigerator in a paper bag for 3‑5 days. Dried mushrooms keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to a year. If kept in the fridge, dried mushrooms may absorb moisture, so a dry environment is preferred.
